source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Metformin lowers blood glucose mainly by:
questions.rationale: Biguanides inhibit hepatic glucose production and increase insulin sensitivity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Antidiabetic Agents (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: Inhibits production of glucose by the liver

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which oral agent stimulates the pancreas to secrete insulin?
questions.rationale: Sulfonylureas (e.g., gliclazide) stimulate beta cells.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Antidiabetic Agents (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: Stimulate beta cell of the pancreas to secrete insulin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Bedtime glucose normal, 3 AM hypoglycemia, then morning hyperglycemia. This is:
questions.rationale: Somogyi: nocturnal hypoglycemia triggers rebound hyperglycemia; reduce evening dose or add snack.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Morning Hyperglycemia (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: a decrease at 2-3 am to hypoglycemic levels

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How is the dawn phenomenon managed?
questions.rationale: Change evening intermediate-acting insulin from dinnertime to bedtime.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Morning Hyperglycemia (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: Change time of injection of evening intermediate-acting insulin from dinnertime to bedtime.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should the insulin vial currently in use be stored?
questions.rationale: In-use vial at room temperature; spares refrigerated; never frozen or in sunlight.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Storing Insulin (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: The insulin vial in use should be kept at room temperature

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should a client prepare a cloudy insulin vial?
questions.rationale: Roll or gently invert to mix without bubbles; inspect for flocculation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Storing Insulin (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: rolling it between the hands

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An NPH insulin vial shows a frosted, whitish coating inside. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Flocculation (frosted whitish coating) means the insulin is altered and should not be used.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Storing Insulin (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: Bottles of intermediate-acting insulin should also be inspected for flocculation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Insulin is absorbed fastest from which site?
questions.rationale: Absorption is fastest in the abdomen, then arm, thigh, hip.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Injection Sites (PDF p. 375)
questions.quote: The speed of absorption is greatest in the abdomen

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A diabetic jogger asks where to inject insulin before running. The nurse advises avoiding:
questions.rationale: Exercising a limb speeds absorption, risking hypoglycemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Injection Sites (PDF p. 375)
questions.quote: Insulin should not be injected into the limb that will be exercised

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Shakiness, sweating, tachycardia, and hunger in a client on insulin indicate:
questions.rationale: Adrenergic symptoms signal mild hypoglycemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoglycemia (PDF p. 375)
questions.quote: Mild hypoglycemia

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A diabetic client is unconscious at home with no IV access. The family should give:
questions.rationale: Glucagon 1 mg SC or IM; never give oral fluids to an unconscious person.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoglycemia Emergency (PDF p. 376)
questions.quote: Injection of glucagon 1mg (subcutaneously or intramuscularly.)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is IV line patency checked before giving 50% dextrose?
options: It is very irritating to veins
questions.rationale: D50W is hypertonic and irritating; infiltration damages tissue.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoglycemia Emergency (PDF p. 376)
questions.quote: Assuring patency of the IV line because (D5OW) is very irritating to veins.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Deep, rapid respirations with fruity breath in a type 1 diabetic indicate:
questions.rationale: Kussmaul breathing and acetone breath compensate for ketoacidosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Diabetic Ketoacidosis (PDF p. 376)
questions.quote: Kussmaul’s respiration – rapid, deep breathing

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the first priority in DKA management?
questions.rationale: Start 0.9% NaCl rehydration; then insulin and potassium as needed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, DKA Management (PDF p. 377)
questions.quote: 0.9% Sodium chloride (normal saline solution)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During DKA treatment with insulin, the nurse closely monitors:
questions.rationale: Insulin and rehydration shift potassium into cells; replace once K is normal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, DKA Electrolytes (PDF p. 377)
questions.quote: Serum potassium level must be monitored frequently.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is the first 50 mL of an insulin drip discarded through the tubing?
questions.rationale: Insulin binds to tubing; flushing saturates binding sites.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, DKA Insulin (PDF p. 377)
questions.quote: Insulin molecules adhere to the inner surface of IV infusion sets

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An elderly type 2 diabetic has glucose 900 mg/dL, no ketones, and severe dehydration. This is:
questions.rationale: HHNS: very high glucose, hyperosmolality, minimal ketones, mainly elderly type 2.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, HHNS (PDF p. 377)
questions.quote: Ketosis is usually minimal or absent

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement about DKA versus HHNS is correct?
questions.rationale: DKA: rapid onset, ketones, acidosis; HHNS: slower over days, normal pH.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, DKA vs HHNS (PDF p. 378)
questions.quote: Slower (over several days)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the functional unit of the kidney?
questions.rationale: About 1 million nephrons per kidney filter, reabsorb, and excrete.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nephron (PDF p. 379)
questions.quote: Anatomic & functional unit of the kidney

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Most water (about 80%) is reabsorbed in the:
questions.rationale: PCT reabsorbs glucose, sodium, and about 80% of water.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nephron (PDF p. 380)
questions.quote: 80% of water (osmosis)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Normal adult glomerular filtration rate is about:
questions.rationale: GFR is about 125 mL/min.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urine Volume Control (PDF p. 380)
questions.quote: Constant (125 ml/min)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Normal adult bladder capacity is about:
questions.rationale: Adult bladder holds 300–500 mL.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Bladder (PDF p. 380)
questions.quote: Capacity of the adult bladder 300-500 mL
